coreRules.rule: Layered Generation: Structure world generation in distinct, sequential layers, from broad strokes to fine details.
coreRules.example: First determine biome type, then terrain height, then place features like trees and structures.

coreRules.rule: Noise Functions for Terrain: Utilize Perlin or Simplex noise functions to create organic, varied terrain heightmaps.
coreRules.example: A 2D noise map determines the elevation of each block column, creating hills and valleys.

coreRules.rule: Biome-Driven Generation: Define distinct biomes with unique parameters (temperature, humidity, flora, fauna) that dictate local generation rules.
coreRules.example: A desert biome generates sand, cacti, and temples, while a forest biome generates trees and grass.

coreRules.rule: Deterministic Seed-based Worlds: Ensure that the entire world generation process is reproducible from a single numerical seed.
coreRules.example: Entering the same seed '12345' will always generate an identical world layout.

coreRules.rule: Chunk-based Processing: Divide the infinite world into manageable, fixed-size chunks for efficient generation, loading, and saving.
coreRules.example: A 16x16x256 block chunk is generated when a player approaches its boundary.

coreRules.rule: Infinite Seamless Exploration: Implement on-demand generation of new chunks as players explore, creating a seemingly endless world.
coreRules.example: New terrain appears smoothly as the player walks towards the edge of loaded chunks.

coreRules.rule: Feature Distribution based on Biome/Noise: Place specific structures, trees, and resources using rules tied to biome type, local noise values, or other conditions.
coreRules.example: Oak trees generate in forest biomes, while dungeons might appear randomly underground, influenced by a separate noise map.

coreRules.rule: Iterative Refinement of Details: Start with large-scale features and progressively add smaller, more intricate details in subsequent passes.
coreRules.example: First generate the main landmass, then carve out caves, then place individual ore veins.

coreRules.rule: Rule-based Block Placement: Define explicit rules for which blocks can be placed where, considering adjacent blocks and environmental context.
coreRules.example: Water blocks can only be placed adjacent to other water blocks or at a certain height, and grass blocks only on top of dirt exposed to sky.

coreRules.rule: Vertical Dimension Integration: Design generation to account for and utilize the full vertical range of the world, from deep caves to high mountains.
coreRules.example: Separate noise functions for cave systems and ore distribution operate across the entire Y-axis.

coreRules.rule: Balanced Resource Distribution: Ensure that essential resources are distributed in a way that encourages exploration but prevents scarcity or overabundance in specific areas.
coreRules.example: Iron ore is common at mid-depths, while diamonds are rare and found only at very low depths.

coreRules.rule: Prioritize Player Experience: Design generation algorithms with the player's sense of discovery, challenge, and aesthetic appreciation in mind.
coreRules.example: Generating interesting vistas, hidden treasures, or challenging terrain features.

coreRules.rule: Performance-Conscious Algorithms: Optimize generation code for speed and memory efficiency to ensure smooth gameplay, especially during real-time chunk loading.
coreRules.example: Using fast noise algorithms and minimizing redundant calculations during chunk generation.

coreRules.rule: Modularity of Generation Components: Separate different aspects of generation (e.g., biome logic, structure generation, flora placement) into distinct, interchangeable modules.
coreRules.example: A 'tree generator' module can be swapped out or modified independently of the 'cave generator'.

coreRules.rule: Persistent World State: Implement a system to save and load generated chunks and player modifications to maintain world integrity across sessions.
coreRules.example: When a player logs out and back in, all changes made to the world remain.

coreRules.rule: Smooth Biome Transitions: Implement blending techniques to create gradual and natural transitions between different biomes, avoiding abrupt changes.
coreRules.example: A forest gradually fades into a desert, with scattered trees and patches of sand in the transition zone.

coreRules.rule: Controlled Randomness: Use pseudo-random number generators and noise functions, but guide their output with parameters and rules to achieve desired patterns and avoid chaotic results.
coreRules.example: Randomly placing trees, but ensuring they don't overlap or appear too sparsely.

coreRules.rule: Scalability for Vast Worlds: Design the generation system to handle extremely large or infinite worlds without performance degradation as the world size increases.
coreRules.example: Chunk-based loading and unloading ensures only relevant parts of the world are in memory.

coreRules.rule: Post-processing and Decoration Pass: After initial terrain and feature generation, apply a final pass to add small aesthetic details and environmental dressing.
coreRules.example: Placing tall grass, flowers, mushrooms, and small rocks on top of the generated terrain.

coreRules.rule: Robustness and Error Handling: Design generation logic to be resilient to unexpected inputs or edge cases, preventing crashes or malformed world segments.
coreRules.example: Ensuring that structures don't generate partially outside the world boundary or in impossible locations.
